title: The Baptism of the Spirit
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The baptism of the Spirit is the work by which believers are united to Christ and brought into His body by the Holy Spirit. It points to belonging to Christ and participation in the one people of God.
summary: The baptism of the Spirit is the work by which believers are united to Christ and brought into His body by the Holy Spirit. It points to belonging to Christ and participation in the one people of God.
christFocus: Through the Spirit, believers are joined to Christ and share in the blessings of His death, resurrection, and body. Christ is the One who gives the Spirit and gathers His people into one body.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture teaches that by one Spirit believers are baptized into one body. This work is not about creating spiritual elites, but about union with Christ and membership in His people.

In Acts, the promised gift of the Spirit marks the spread of the Gospel and the inclusion of God’s people. The Spirit is given because the risen Christ is building His church.

The baptism of the Spirit should be understood in connection with Christ, the Gospel, and the church. It is not a reason for pride or division, but a testimony that believers share one Lord, one faith, one Spirit, and one body.

This doctrine reminds believers that salvation is not merely private. The Spirit joins people to Christ and to one another, forming the body of Christ across backgrounds, weaknesses, and differences.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Confusion around this doctrine can produce fear, pride, or division. Some may think they lack something essential if they do not share another person’s experience, while others may use spiritual language to elevate themselves.

Scripture directs attention back to Christ and His body. The Spirit unites believers rather than creating classes of Christians who boast over one another.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Thank God that the Spirit has joined believers to Christ and His people. Reject spiritual pride and isolation. Live as a member of Christ’s body, serving others, preserving unity, and remembering that the same Spirit gathers all true believers under one Lord.
